I drove for about 30 minutes in city traffic with off-policy model v4, using E2E experimental mode and SCC-V enabled.

Lane centering was excellent, and with SCC-V active, it slowed down appropriately for curves and handled them smoothly and safely.

With SCC-V turned off, it tends to take curves at the set speed without reducing speed, which feels a bit risky.

Compared to WMI v12 / CD210, it was more hesitant to start moving when the lead vehicle pulled away, and I had to intervene a few times due to the delayed response.
did you feel like it usually drove an appropriate speed for the road?
like you didn’t have to gas press as much to get it up to speed or brake to stop it from being crazy

It accelerated smoothly up to the set speed (60 km/h in city traffic) and maintained it consistently. I don’t have any complaints about its cruising speed behavior.

It seems to strictly follow the user-set speed, so it doesn’t proactively adjust based on road width or context. The driver needs to set an appropriate speed for the conditions.

From harald at today's OP dev call: "Off Policy model is a refactor, where a really smart model is trained off policy, not in simulation. This model can predict very well what is going to happen in the scene, but cannot act or recover from its own mistakes. The two models are seperated in the sense that off-policy model is giving a off-policy prediction potential and where driving policy giving a on-policy recovery potential. Makes traning more efficient and the models more debuggable.

My interpretation: The two models run in tandem, off policy picks the plan on where to go and how, On-policy then helps execute's off-policy's plan by correcting mistakes the mistakes off-policy makes. I guess this how its a plan plus, we can strenghen how much the on-policy wants to correct off-policys mistakes. Too much correction leads to ping pong. Too little correction leads to drifting out of lane.

I think the idea of 2 separate models is an issue. It seems like as long as the car is centered in it's lane everything is fine but as soon as the car veers off center it starts correcting. If it ever over corrects back to center the other model doesn't cancel out the lateral velocity and ends up hitting the other side of the lane. This is an unstable situation that amplifies. After testing WMI you can clearly see it centers in the lane and then also cancels out its lateral velocity. On OPMv4 at about 35mph pull the steering wheel towards the edge of the lane and let go. Increasing plan plus control to 1.2-1.5 makes this way worse. Even at 0.9 it was still pretty bad.

I like the aggressiveness, but I ended up going back to CD210. With v4 it tends to speed up too much when the new lead is further ahead, and it  leads to some rubber banding. For example, when switching lanes or if someone takes an exit and the new lead is 5–10 car lengths ahead, the system detects the new lead correctly, but I can tell I’m going at least ~10 mph faster than them. Eventually it hits the brakes but a bit too much so it overcorrects, so the cycle repeats. It does eventually settle itself out, but there's only so much I can take. 

Lane changes though 10/10 on assertiveness and speed.
